newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Moscow repeats dislike of Ukraine-NATO exercises.
newsitem.headline: Moscow repeats dislike of Ukraine-NATO exercises.

text.p: Russia has not changed its negative view of plans for NATO-led naval exercises off Ukraine's Crimean peninsula in August despite its deal with Kiev on the Black Sea Fleet, the Kremlin spokesman said on Friday.

"We see certain anti-Russian hints in these exercises," spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said, referring to the "Sea-Breeze" exercises which will include the Ukrainian navy. Russia declined an invitation to take part.

"We consider the exercises to be counter-productive and that they cannot contribute to the security of the Black Sea region," he told a news briefing after Russian President Boris Yeltsin arrived in Ukraine to sign a friendship treaty.
Under the deal aimed at ending a protracted dispute over sharing out the disputed fleet, Russia won a 20-year lease of the Crimean port of Sevastopol.
Moscow has bitterly opposed Ukraine's plans to host NATO exercises off the Russian-populated peninsula.
